name: Software Engineer
tagline: Land a new-grad software engineering job and thrive in your first team.
description: The full-time version of the SWE track. Learn one language in depth (Python) plus JavaScript and TypeScript, the computer science and data structures and algorithms that interview loops test to medium level, and object-oriented and system design. Then build the engineering practice teams expect: testing, debugging, code review, APIs and databases, security, concurrency, CI/CD and the cloud. It ends with how engineering teams work day to day and how to grow once you are hired.
outcome: You can pass a new-grad interview loop (medium coding problems, an object-oriented design round, a basic system design discussion and behavioral questions), and on the job you can own a feature end to end: design it, build it with tests, get it reviewed, ship it through CI/CD and support it in production.

stages.title: One language deeply, a second well
stages.summary: Python from the basics to decorators, generators, typing and asyncio, then JavaScript and TypeScript for the web side of a codebase.
stages.milestone: Write idiomatic, typed Python without looking up syntax, and read a TypeScript codebase comfortably.

stages.title: Computer science core
stages.summary: How data is represented and code runs, Big-O, the core data structures and algorithms, and operating systems.
stages.milestone: Pick the right data structure for a task, state the complexity of your code, and explain what the OS does when your program runs.

stages.title: Data structures and algorithms I
stages.summary: The interview playbook, then arrays and strings, hash maps, two pointers, sliding window, stacks and queues, binary search and linked lists.
stages.milestone: Recognize the pattern in a new problem within a few minutes and solve easy problems cleanly while talking through them.

stages.title: Data structures and algorithms II
stages.summary: Trees, heaps, graphs, backtracking, dynamic programming, greedy and intervals, bit manipulation, tries, union-find and prefix sums.
stages.milestone: Solve medium tree, graph and dynamic programming problems in about 30 minutes and explain the trade-offs.

stages.title: Engineering craft
stages.summary: The shell, git in a team, the Python toolchain, testing, debugging, clean code, object-oriented design and design patterns.
stages.milestone: Ship a tested, typed package through CI, and talk through an object-oriented design such as a parking lot in 40 minutes.

stages.title: The web stack: APIs, data and security
stages.summary: SQL and database design, HTTP and REST, building APIs in Python with FastAPI and SQLAlchemy, secure coding, and enough HTML, CSS and React to ship a full-stack feature.
stages.milestone: Build and test an authenticated API backed by a database, put a small React front end on it, and review someone else's API code for security problems.

stages.title: Concurrency, cloud and scale
stages.summary: Threads, locks and async, containers, CI/CD and the cloud, and system design from the basics to an interview-ready approach.
stages.milestone: Deploy your API through a pipeline, and talk through the design of a URL shortener or news feed with numbers and trade-offs.

stages.title: Get hired, then thrive
stages.summary: Resume, portfolio and behavioral interviews, then how teams plan, review, document, handle incidents and grow engineers.
stages.milestone: Applications in flight with a one-page resume and story bank, and a clear picture of how to be a reliable teammate from week one.

resources.title: Tech Interview Handbook
resources.note: A free guide to the whole new-grad loop, including negotiation, which matters more for a full-time offer.

resources.title: NeetCode roadmap
resources.note: Hundreds more problems organized by the same patterns, each with a video, for volume practice.

resources.title: Pramp
resources.note: Mock interviews with other candidates, to practice coding while someone watches.

resources.title: The Missing Semester
resources.note: Free MIT lectures on the shell, editors, debugging and version control that make you faster every day.

resources.title: Teach Yourself Computer Science
resources.note: A curated list of free books and lectures for going deeper into any CS area this path introduces.

resources.title: Backend Developer Roadmap
resources.note: A community map of backend skills, useful for choosing what to learn after your first job starts.

resources.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
resources.note: Paid classic on the habits of effective engineers, a natural follow-up to Working as a Software Engineer.

resources.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
resources.note: Paid book; the deep dive on databases, replication and distributed systems behind system design rounds.
